newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Pannonplast bucks Budapest bearish trend.
newsitem.headline: Pannonplast bucks Budapest bearish trend.

text.p: Hungarian share prices closed mostly lower on the Budapest Stock Exchange on Tuesday, matching the trend on European bourses which were hit by political worries over Iraq, traders said.
The BUX index ended at 3,513.78 points, down 60.87, bringing the index down from Monday's all-time record. Spot share turnover totalled 1.21 billion forints.
However, the Budapest bourse was declining also because it became overheated in the past two days and some investors decided to take profits, believing the market was vulnerable.

"Strangely, Hungary bucked the falling trend that Europe saw in the past two days," said Robert Agoston of Daewoo Securities. "And they fell (in the past two days) not because of the Iraqi crisis but due to fears of U.S. interest rate hike," he said.
"But the Iraqi news had definitely to do with today's falls in Europe," Agoston said.

Plastics industrial Pannonplast defied the bearish trend and continued to rise once again to new highs after Pannonplast's announcement last Friday that it had acquired Kaposplast Kft. Pannonplast soared to close at 5,100 forints, up 200.
Traders said movements on the Wall Street will have a key impact on Budapest this week.
